A woman who craves constant control and consistency is a woman who experienced a lot of chaos as a child 

#healthybodyhealthymind #wellnessjourney #healthy #mindfulness
transcript: A woman who craves constant control and consistency is a woman who experienced a lot of chaos as a child. She never knew which version of her parents would appear. Warm one moment, angry the next, present one day, absent the following. Her nervous system learned early, uncertainty is danger. So she adapted, she learned to anticipate, to manage, to stay two steps ahead. If she could control the environment, maybe she could avoid the pain. She became independent too soon, responsible before it was fair, strong in ways children should never have to be. For some, the chaos went deeper, boundaries were broken, safety was taken. Control became the only form of protection and now, in adulthood, her body still remembers. She analyzes messages, she senses subtle shifts, she struggles to relax into trust. Not because she is difficult, but because her nervous system is still living in a world that once felt unsafe. That control is not ego, it is a frightened inner child trying to survive. And healing does not begin by managing everyone else. It begins when she turns inward and meets the little girl who learned control instead of safety. She is not too much, she is still waiting to feel safe. This is not about fixing yourself, it is about meeting the part of you that learned to survive. The 30-day healing journey is there for that process. You can find it in my profile.
